statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the following holds. Define a valid refueling plan of k stops (for 0 <= k <= len(stations)) as: either k = 0 and start_fuel >= target, or k >= 1 and there exist indices 0 <= i_1 < i_2 < ... < i_k < len(stations) such that (1) start_fuel >= stations[i_1][0], (2) for every j with 1 <= j < k, start_fuel + sum_{m=1}^{j} stations[i_m][1] >= stations[i_{j+1}][0], and (3) start_fuel + sum_{m=1}^{k} stations[i_m][1] >= target. Then r is the smallest k in {0, 1, ..., len(stations)} for which a valid refueling plan of k stops exists; if no such k exists, r = -1.
preconditions: The inputs satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= target <= 10^9, 1 <= start_fuel <= 10^9, 0 <= len(stations) <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < len(stations), len(stations[i]) = 2, 1 <= stations[i][0] < target, 1 <= stations[i][1] < 10^9; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(stations)-1, stations[i][0] < stations[i+1][0].
